answer: On a karst wall, each identity writes its claim with a quill while a sparrow nests above it. The ink fades as the cave drips, and the sparrow calls when a mark grows faint. Every identity backs its claim with a 950,000 POA stake and re-inks it when the sparrow calls. Two marks re-inked at the same drip belong to one operator: both rewards burn, both stakes pass to honest peers, and the operator pays a 650,000 POA fine per fake. One fake costs 1,600,000 POA, and seven fakes cost 11,200,000 POA before any payout clears.
